learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to perform and interpret the results of basic principles, methods and fundamental concepts of material and component testing (stress state, tensile tests, impact tests, hardness tests, single-stage fatigue tests…) for characterizing materials and components.
evaluate influencing factors such as notches, residual stresses and temperature on material and component strength.
perform and evaluate stress analyses with strain gauges on simple geometries.
distinguish between destructive and non-destructive testing methods and their application possibilities.
analyze different types of failure and the resulting damage.
Through participation in the practical course, students can perform and evaluate various material tests themselves.
document experiments in a group by dividing tasks and jointly planning and coordinating the necessary work steps.
critically evaluate and interpret their own results from the practical experiments.

syllabus_topics: Component testing and Full Scale Test
assessment_rules: The module grade is based 100% on the graded exam for Component Testing (2 LP). The Lab Course Component Testing (2 LP) is ungraded but requires a lab course entry test, pre-colloquium, and lab course reports as prerequisites for credit.
